openQuestions:
STRUCTURAL RESTORATION BLOCKED ON ROUTE ADJUDICATION, not an editorial judgment. The introduction to PART SIX, the running prose between the part label Contact With the World and the first chapter heading beneath it, compiles into a chapter-start section with its own public route. Restoring the baseline's fuller introduction revives a section whose route was retired, and attempting it broke the build for this part. The introduction has therefore been reverted to its pre-edit state byte for byte and no part introduction anywhere in this volume was touched. Reassigning a canonical route and a reviewed successor is an author-facing continuity decision and this pass has no standing to make it.

WHAT STANDS NOW:

Providence would meet laws, markets, institutions, critics, partners, and people who do not share its premises. Part VI examines co-optation, scaling pressure, failure, and invitation. It makes no promise that the proposed defenses are sufficient.

WHAT THE BASELINE HAS, punctuation already repaired so it can be pasted in one edit once the route decision is made:

The world Providence is being built to help transform is not waiting. It is proceeding according to its own logic: the logic of extraction, of short-horizon optimization, of coordination architectures evolved for conditions that no longer obtain but that remain deeply embedded in the institutions, the economic systems, and the cognitive frameworks through which most human beings navigate their lives. Providence will encounter that world. The encounter is not avoidable. It is designable.

Volume III's intellectual discipline was, appropriately, primarily inward-looking: establishing what Providence would have to be before engaging the question of how it would relate to what already exists. Volume IV's first five parts have been similarly focused on the internal architecture: the sequencing, the economics, the governance, the technology, the human development. Part VI turns outward. It examines what happens when the architecture, however well designed, meets the world as it actually is rather than as the architecture presupposes it should be.

The three chapters of Part VI are the most honest in the book. They do not promise that the encounter will be navigable, only that it must be prepared for. They do not promise that the architecture will survive contact with the world intact, only that it has been designed with enough constitutional resilience to make survival possible. And they close with an invitation that earns the right to be extended because the preceding twenty-one chapters have been honest about what the invitation actually involves.

WHAT THE CURRENT TEXT LOSES: the account of the world as proceeding on its own logic rather than waiting, the claim that the encounter is not avoidable but is designable, and the statement that these three chapters are the most honest in the book.

TO RESTORE: the prose change and the continuity change must land together. The section id minted by the restored introduction needs a canonical route and a reviewed successor recorded in publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json in the same edit.

The section's measured word count exceeds the baseline's because the shipped rank caution is kept alongside the restored responsibilities, and because the closing interlude is counted here with the coda heading gone.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.
